statement: A general complementary affine linear section of St(3,3) has 16 complex points.

source.location: Theorem 1.1; Table 1, printed page 7, row k=3, column n=3

notes:
Source specialization: Table 1, row k=3, column n=3.

For k=n, St(n,n)=O(n) has two isomorphic determinant components, so its degree is twice the SO(n) degree computed by Brandt et al.; Brysiewicz–Gesmundo explicitly credit that predecessor. Their general Stiefel formula is a separate result.

Madeline Brandt; Juliette Bruce; Taylor Brysiewicz; Robert Krone; Elina Robeva, The Degree of SO(n,C) (2017, article ID brandt_2017_degree_so). Supporting degree or irreducibility input for the catalogue deduction, retained here as background bibliography.
